$comment: TWO SETS OF NUMBERS, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS.
`bauerSource` is measured from eight public-domain John Bauer scans on Wikimedia
Commons (Tuvstarr gazing into the tarn; Annu sitter Tuvstarr kvar; The Princess
and the Trolls; Little Bianca Maria; Elk & Cottongrass; A Forest Troll NMB 342;
En kvall vid midsommartid; Sagoprinsessan; Humpe in the Woods).
Those absolute values CANNOT be chased directly. Bauer is watercolour on aged
paper: paper-white shows through every wash, which lifts median luma and
suppresses HSV saturation. A dark digital night render is a different medium and
will never sit in that band without being washed out. Measured proof: the
project's own concept reference (a painterly night forest, and the image this
theme was built toward) scores p50 16.8 / sat p50 0.59 - it fails the raw Bauer
band exactly as our render does, and in the same direction.
`targets` below are therefore operational, derived from what IS transferable
between media: top-end compression, and the concentration of the bright note.
Both are calibrated against the concept reference, which is same-medium.
See docs/STILLWATER_BAUER_MASTERPIECE_PLAN_2026-07.md.
saturation.p50 is a BAND, not a ceiling: driving chroma to zero scores well
against the raw Bauer scans yet reads as washed-out grey in this medium.
Bauer is muted, not colourless - moss green, ochre and blue-grey all survive.
bright.fraction has a FLOOR as well as a ceiling: a frame with no bright
note at all scores well on every other metric and is compositionally dead.

bauerSource.note: Provenance only. Do not gate on these.

conceptReference.note: Same-medium calibration target. This is what we actually chase.

diagnostics.note: Derived from a reference with no strong specular water lane. Stillwater's moon path is a large bright region BY DESIGN, so these two cannot be met without a shoulder that also crushes the spirit. Tracked, not gated - revisit if the painterly pass (Wave 4) changes the top end.
